answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy behaves like a voyage toll paid in ferrous proof rather than in promises: every new identity must burn a small, non-refundable deposit of compute and stake, and that deposit only becomes usable once unrelated peers have vouched for it across several epochs. Registering ten thousand sock puppets therefore costs ten thousand paid proofs plus ten thousand separate audits, while an honest participant needs just one. A single ember of real reputation takes months to earn but is trivial to strip, so faking scale always stays more expensive than joining honestly.
